texts: Staphylococcus aureus mitral endocarditis with a 1.5 cm vegetation, severe regurgitation and an annular abscess needs early surgery.
After a small ischaemic stroke that has fully resolved, the best step is to operate as soon as a repeat CT shows no cerebral haemorrhage.
An abscess will not heal with antibiotics alone, and the large mobile vegetation threatens further emboli.
Heparin on bypass can turn a haemorrhagic stroke into a disaster, so bleeding must be excluded; a small ischaemic stroke without haemorrhage is no reason to delay.
Six or eight weeks of antibiotics first, or waiting two weeks, risks new emboli and heart failure.
